title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Equal
summary: Given an array arr of length n where each element is defined as (2 * i) + 1, you can perform operations to make all elements equal by selecting two indices x and y and adjusting arr[x] and arr[y] by -1 and +1 respectively.
statement: Given an array arr of length n where each element is defined as (2 * i) + 1, you can perform operations to make all elements equal by selecting two indices x and y and adjusting arr[x] and arr[y] by -1 and +1 respectively. The task is to find the minimum number of such operations needed to achieve an equal array.
constraints: The conceptual array is arr[i]=2*i+1 for i from zero through n-1.
One operation decreases one element and increases another by one; return the minimum operations to make all values equal.
hints: The invariant total sum makes the final value equal to n.
Each operation can fix one unit of deficit below n using one unit of surplus above n.
Sum the deficits of the lower half, which simplifies to floor(n²/4).
Symmetry guarantees equal total deficit and surplus, so that many transfers are necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: Array 1,3,5 becomes all threes in two transfers.
Moving units toward the mean value six requires nine operations.
